reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard Arch Linux package that fetches source from the official upstream (Debian Salsa) with pinned SHA256 checksums and applies local patches using standard `patch` commands. There is no execution of fetched content, no suspicious network requests, and no malicious code in the build scripts. The patches are standard bugfixes and feature additions consistent with the package's description.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from an API error in the qwen3 model when processing .gitignore, causing it to return an 'inconclusive' verdict. coverage_issues: All models incorrectly skipped .patch files, misidentifying them as binary files. Patches are text files and are critical to review since they are applied during the build process.
The qwen3 model experienced an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing .gitignore, which incorrectly forced the entire package audit to an 'inconclusive' state.
false_negatives: The audit tool failed to read and analyze the .patch files, missing the opportunity to verify that the applied diffs do not contain malicious C code injections.
learnings: Fix file type detection: The tool incorrectly classifies .patch files as binary. It should rely on file extensions or content sniffing to correctly identify text-based patches and pass them to the LLM.
